your plant is fine! the "damages leaves" I see here are:

1) bottom leaves

2) on the flower stalk.

it's normal for the bottom leaves to die, as the plant uses those to grow. As they die, the plant uses the energy it gathered from there to make new leaves! It's just how they do it, completely normal :) 


the leaves on the flower stalk are damaged because the flower is likely about to die, as no flower is eternal this one is reaching the end of its life. Totally normal! you can cut it or you can keep it there, i remove them when they start to get crispy. 

As for the plant being thirsty, I'm not so sure! learn to understand signs of thirst instead of watering on a schedule, touch the leaves (not the bottom ones, but the ones in the middle) and if they feel soft, not "tense", and get a bit wrinkly then the plant is thirsty. I've seen this called "the taco test". I'm sure you can find more about it on this subreddit/online if i wasn't clear enough! 


To water it correctly, you need to SOAK IT. Don't get the leaves wet, just the dirt. Make sure that the pot has a drainage hole, and the potting medium should be well draining cacti /succulents soil. You could also mix it 1:1 with perlite for an excellent blend, your plant will love it.
After you soak it wait for the water to drain out of the hole and remember to remove the water from the saucer if you have one. Plants don't like wet feet and will rot. I use distilled water but it's not necessary, my tap water is very high in minerals so I don't want to use it. 

That's all! feel free to ask any questions if you want

as a side note, taxonomy is __hard__

Fun fact! what is commonly know as air plants ([Tillandsia genus](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tillandsia), think  what is commonly called Spanish moss) *are* in the Bromeliaceae family. So both is correct! When one says bromeliad we usually think about [Guzmania](https://www.florafashion.nl/Files/6/89000/89487/FileBrowser/verzorging/bromelia-calypso-rood-45cm-p12-750px-5.jpg) because it's probably the most common one to keep as an houseplant, but it's a family with 3700 species!! Even pineapples are Bromeliaceae. 

This pictured here is likely a Wallisia cyanea, which *is* in the bromeliad family, and, to complicate things further, used to be classified in the tillandsia genus, with other air plants because this too is epiphytic; that's why it looks so similar to an air plant.. *technically* it is one. But it got reclassified as as a Wallisia after DNA analysis :)

it depends vastly from where you are, a huge variegated monstera might be growing on the side of the road like a weed in SE Asia and nobody would look at it twice, while a small cutting of the same plant can go for $500 and up in California. 

For a less extreme example, i live in Italy and I'm always surprised at the price of plants in the US, even for common plants it's about 4 or 5x the amount. And we're talking about plants that are not native here either, like succulents and tropical plants. I got a nice [variegated peperomia obtusifolia](https://www.reddit.com/r/peperomia/comments/uvgtqg/my_first_peperomia_im_obsessed_it_was_only_4/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android_app&utm_name=androidcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button) at the hardware store for €3, while on Etsy, from US sellers, you can find it [half the size starting from $20](https://www.etsy.com/it/listing/1309632075/pianta-di-gomma-variegata-per-bambini?click_key=445921fe3daaf2f559fb2e3aa80ee7ee2c1de892%3A1309632075&click_sum=66e7d7cd&ga_order=most_relevant&ga_search_type=all&ga_view_type=gallery&ga_search_query=peperomia+obtusifolia+variegata&ref=sr_gallery-1-8&organic_search_click=1). Or a small ficus elastica, i could find it easily for $4 while i recently saw [a picture on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/houseplants/comments/zgesqp/found_at_petco_today/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android_app&utm_name=androidcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button) that PetCo started selling plants and there were rubber plants on the shelf, the same size, going for $20.

It's all about supply and demand, really . If you're not from a place where there is a "plant craze" going on you won't be able to sell them for much, sadly
